name: Eminem
milestone_by_age_26: Released The Slim Shady LP on February 23, 1999, which debuted at #2 on the Billboard 200 with 283,000 first-week sales and was certified platinum by April 1999.
early_history_summary: Eminem began rapping in Detroit clubs at age 14 and dropped out of high school at 17. He signed with FBT Productions (the Bass Brothers) in 1992, released the commercially unsuccessful Infinite in 1996, and then crafted the Slim Shady EP in 1997, which caught the attention of Dr. Dre and led to his major-label debut.
family_context_summary: Born to a teenage single mother in poverty in St. Joseph, Missouri; father abandoned the family when Eminem was 18 months old. He was raised in poverty in Detroit's working-class neighborhoods and was bullied as one of few white kids in a Black neighborhood.
primary_early_advantage_tags: poverty-driven urgency, Detroit hip-hop immersion, Bass Brothers mentorship, exceptional verbal talent
evidence_summary: Eminem grew up in poverty in Detroit with a single teenage mother and no father present. He began rapping at 14 and dropped out of high school, spending years honing his craft in Detroit's underground hip-hop scene. The Bass Brothers discovered him and provided studio access and production mentorship, leading to the failed Infinite album (1996) and then the Slim Shady EP (1997), which Dr. Dre championed into a major-label deal. The Slim Shady LP (1999) debuted at #2 on the Billboard 200 and went platinum within months, all while Eminem was 26.
starting_point: Born to a teenage single mother in St. Joseph, Missouri in 1972; father abandoned the family before age 2; raised in poverty in Detroit's working-class neighborhoods.
current_position: One of the best-selling music artists of all time with over 220 million records sold; estimated net worth approximately $250 million; still active in music.

trajectory.event: Released debut album Infinite through Web Entertainment; it was a commercial failure selling approximately 1,000 copies.
Released The Slim Shady LP, which debuted at #2 on the Billboard 200 and was certified platinum by April 1999, launching mainstream fame.
Released The Marshall Mathers LP, which sold 1.76 million copies in its first week, becoming the fastest-selling solo album in US history.
Released The Eminem Show and starred in 8 Mile, winning the Academy Award for Best Original Song for 'Lose Yourself'.
Released The Marshall Mathers LP 2, which won the Grammy Award for Best Rap Album.
Released The Death of Slim Shady (Coup de Grace), his 12th studio album, which debuted at #1 on the Billboard 200.

name: Berit Aunli
milestone_by_age_26: Won bronze medal in the 4x5 km relay at the 1980 Winter Olympics in Lake Placid at age 23, her first international championship medal; also won 11 individual Norwegian national championships between 1977 and 1982.
early_history_summary: Born into a prominent Norwegian skiing family, Aunli's father was a national champion and national team coach. She began training seriously in 1975 and won her first national championships in 1977, breaking through internationally at the 1978 World Championships with sixth-place finishes before winning Olympic bronze in 1980.
family_context_summary: Born into a skiing family in Norway; her father Kristen Kvello was the 1957 Norwegian champion in the 50 km, served as national coach from 1958-64, and was a FIS cross-country committee member.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a Norwegian national cross-country skiing champion, national team coach, and FIS committee member, providing deep domain expertise and connections in the sport.
primary_early_advantage_tags: ski family, father national champion and coach, Norwegian skiing ecosystem, early specialization
evidence_summary: Berit Aunli was born into Norway's cross-country skiing elite; her father was a national champion, national coach, and FIS committee member. She began serious training at 18 and quickly dominated Norwegian national championships from 1977. Her father's deep involvement in the sport provided coaching, connections, and immersion in the Norwegian skiing pipeline, which is the world's strongest cross-country system. She won Olympic bronze at 23 and went on to win three World Championship golds in 1982.
starting_point: Born in 1956 into a prominent Norwegian cross-country skiing family; father was the 1957 Norwegian 50 km champion and national team coach from 1958-64.
current_position: Retired from competitive skiing in 1986; runs a sports shop with husband Ove Aunli in Kyrksaeteroa, Norway.

trajectory.event: Competed in her first senior season and first Winter Olympics in Innsbruck, placing 17th in the 5 km and 18th in the 10 km.
Placed 6th in both the 10 km and 20 km at the World Ski Championships in Lahti, the best results among Norwegian women.
Won her first international medal, a bronze in the 4x5 km relay, at the Lake Placid Winter Olympics.
Won three gold medals and a silver at the FIS Nordic World Ski Championships in Oslo and claimed the inaugural overall Cross-Country World Cup title.
Won Olympic gold in the 4x5 km relay and silver in the 5 km at the Sarajevo Winter Olympics.
Retired from competitive skiing after her final season on the World Cup circuit.

name: Devi Shetty
milestone_by_age_26: Completed MBBS from Kasturba Medical College in 1979 at age 26, which is a standard medical degree rather than an exceptional independently verifiable milestone; his major achievements including founding Narayana Health (2001), performing India's first neonatal heart surgery (1992), and receiving the Padma Shri (2004) all came after age 36.
early_history_summary: Born in a village in Karnataka, India, Shetty was inspired to become a heart surgeon as a schoolboy after learning about Christiaan Barnard. He completed his MBBS in 1979 and MS in General Surgery in 1982, then trained at Guy's Hospital in London before returning to India in 1989.
family_context_summary: Born in Kinnigoli, a village in Karnataka, India; eighth of nine children of a businessman father who encouraged all children to become professionals.
evidence_summary: Devi Shetty completed his MBBS at age 26, which is a standard medical qualification rather than an exceptional milestone. His career-defining achievements, including founding Narayana Health, performing India's first neonatal heart surgery, and receiving the Padma Bhushan, all occurred well after age 36.

name: Belle Delphine
milestone_by_age_26: Went viral in July 2019 for selling 'gamer girl bathwater,' amassing 4.5 million Instagram followers and becoming a globally recognized internet personality at age 19, covered by Rolling Stone and Business Insider.
early_history_summary: Born in South Africa and raised in the UK, Delphine dropped out of school at 14 due to bullying. She began posting cosplay and makeup content on Instagram in 2015-2016, gradually building an audience before her provocative e-girl persona exploded in popularity in 2018-2019.
family_context_summary: Born in Cape Town, South Africa; moved to the UK as a child. Dropped out of secondary school at age 14 due to bullying and worked odd jobs including nannying before finding online fame.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Instagram platform, e-girl culture wave, early content creation, viral marketing instinct
evidence_summary: Belle Delphine grew up in South Africa and the UK, dropping out of school at 14 due to bullying. She began posting cosplay content on Instagram around 2015-2016 and gradually built an audience through her distinctive e-girl persona. Her July 2019 bathwater stunt went globally viral, covered by Rolling Stone and Business Insider, making her one of the internet's most recognizable personalities at age 19. Her success was driven by platform-native distribution and an intuitive grasp of viral internet culture.
starting_point: Born in Cape Town, South Africa in 1999; moved to the UK as a child; dropped out of school at 14 due to bullying and worked odd jobs including nannying before finding online fame.
current_position: Active internet personality and OnlyFans creator; reportedly earning over $1 million per month from content; estimated net worth in the millions.

trajectory.event: Began posting cosplay and makeup content on Instagram, gradually building an audience.
Launched her Patreon and developed her distinctive e-girl persona, rapidly growing her Instagram following.
Went viral for selling 'gamer girl bathwater,' reaching 4.5 million Instagram followers before her account was banned.
Returned to social media after a hiatus and launched an OnlyFans account, reportedly earning over $1 million per month.
Returned to Twitter and other platforms after another hiatus, continuing her internet persona.

name: Maia Chiburdanidze
milestone_by_age_26: Became the sixth Women's World Chess Champion in 1978 at age 17 by defeating Nona Gaprindashvili, the youngest ever at the time, and held the title until 1991.
early_history_summary: Chiburdanidze learned chess from her older brother at age 8 in Kutaisi, Georgian SSR. She won her debut international tournament at Brasov at age 13, became USSR girls' champion at 15, was awarded the Woman Grandmaster title at 16, and won the world championship at 17.
family_context_summary: Born in Kutaisi, Georgian SSR; chess was very popular in her family. Her older brother Reziko taught her to play at age 8. The family moved to Tbilisi so she could receive better chess training at the chess schools there.
parent_family_domain_summary: Chess was very popular in her family; her older brother taught her to play at age 8. The family relocated to Tbilisi to support her chess development at better chess schools.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Soviet chess system, Georgian chess tradition, early prodigy, family chess culture, Tbilisi chess schools
evidence_summary: Maia Chiburdanidze was a chess prodigy from Kutaisi, Georgian SSR, who learned the game from her brother at age 8. She could read at age 3 and showed exceptional cognitive ability early. Her family moved to Tbilisi to give her access to better chess training. The Soviet chess pipeline and Georgia's strong women's chess tradition (exemplified by her predecessor Gaprindashvili) provided the elite ecosystem. She won the world championship at 17, becoming the youngest Women's World Chess Champion ever at that time.
starting_point: Born in 1961 in Kutaisi, Georgian SSR; chess was popular in her family and her older brother taught her to play at age 8; the family relocated to Tbilisi to support her chess development.
current_position: Retired from competitive chess; lives alone near Tbilisi, Georgia, tending to her garden.

trajectory.event: Won her debut international tournament in Brasov, Romania, demonstrating exceptional early talent.
Became USSR girls' champion and finished second in the Tbilisi Women's Interzonal, qualifying for the world championship cycle.
Defeated Nona Gaprindashvili to become the sixth Women's World Chess Champion, the youngest in history at that time.
Became the second woman in history to be awarded the FIDE Grandmaster title.
Successfully defended her world championship title for the fourth time by defeating Nana Ioseliani in Telavi.
Lost the world championship title to Xie Jun of China, ending her 13-year reign.
Won her ninth team gold medal at the Women's Chess Olympiad, her final major international appearance.

name: Renzo Piano
milestone_by_age_26: No material, independently verifiable milestone by age 26 found; he was still an architecture student at the Polytechnic University of Milan, graduating in 1964 at age 27. His first major international recognition came with the 1970 Osaka Expo structure at age 32-33, and the Centre Pompidou competition win in 1971 at age 34.
early_history_summary: Born into a family of builders in Genoa, Italy, Piano studied architecture at the University of Florence and Polytechnic University of Milan, graduating in 1964. He then worked for Louis Kahn in Philadelphia and Z.S. Mackowsky in London before forming his own firm.
family_context_summary: Born in Genoa, Italy, into a family of builders; his grandfather created a masonry enterprise expanded by his father and uncles into the firm Fratelli Piano, which prospered after WWII constructing houses and factories.
parent_family_domain_summary: Family of builders in Genoa; father and uncles ran Fratelli Piano, a construction and building materials firm, providing early exposure to construction and architecture.
evidence_summary: Renzo Piano was still an architecture student at age 26, graduating from the Polytechnic University of Milan in 1964 at age 27. His first international recognition came with the 1970 Osaka Expo structure at age 32-33, and his career-defining Centre Pompidou competition win came in 1971 at age 34. No material milestone by age 26 was found.

name: Benedict Anderson
milestone_by_age_26: No material, independently verifiable milestone by age 26 found; he was completing his undergraduate studies at King's College Cambridge and beginning graduate work at Cornell University. His influential 'Cornell Paper' was written around 1965 at age 29, and his landmark book Imagined Communities was published in 1983 at age 47.
early_history_summary: Born in Kunming, China to an Anglo-Irish family, Anderson was educated at Eton College and King's College Cambridge before moving to Cornell University for his PhD in government studies, which he completed in 1967. He became a leading scholar of Southeast Asian politics and nationalism.
family_context_summary: Born in Kunming, China to an Anglo-Irish father who was an official with Chinese Maritime Customs and an English mother. The family moved to California in 1941 and then to Ireland in 1945. He was educated at Eton College and Cambridge.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a colonial customs official in China; family had Anglo-Irish academic and administrative background. Brother Perry Anderson was a prominent historian.
evidence_summary: Benedict Anderson was still a student at age 26, completing his BA at Cambridge and beginning graduate work at Cornell. His influential 'Cornell Paper' on the 1965 Indonesian coup was written at age 29, and his landmark book Imagined Communities was published at age 47. No material milestone by age 26 was found.

name: Andrea Pirlo
milestone_by_age_26: Won the Serie B title with Brescia in 1997 at age 18, earning promotion to Serie A; had already made his Serie A debut at 16 as Brescia's youngest ever debutant on May 21, 1995.
early_history_summary: Born into a wealthy family in Flero, Brescia, Pirlo joined the Brescia youth sector in 1992 and was promoted to the senior squad by coach Mircea Lucescu at age 15. He made his Serie A debut at 16 and helped Brescia win the Serie B title in 1997 before signing for Inter Milan in 1998.
family_context_summary: Born into a wealthy family in Flero, Brescia, Italy; father Luigi founded Elg Steel, a metal trading company. The family net worth is estimated at 10-20 million euros.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a successful steel businessman, not in football; however, the family wealth provided a strong financial safety net for pursuing a football career.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Italian football system, Brescia youth academy, wealthy family, early promotion by Lucescu, Lombardy football culture
evidence_summary: Andrea Pirlo was born into a wealthy family in Flero, Brescia, with his father running a successful steel trading business. He joined Brescia's youth sector at 13 and was promoted to the senior squad at 15 by coach Mircea Lucescu, who recognized his exceptional talent. He made his Serie A debut at 16, Brescia's youngest ever, and won the Serie B title at 18. His family's wealth provided a strong safety net, while the Italian football pipeline and Brescia's academy provided the elite development pathway.
starting_point: Born in 1979 in Flero, Brescia, Italy, into a wealthy family; father Luigi founded Elg Steel, a metal trading company, with family net worth estimated at 10-20 million euros.
current_position: Retired from professional football in 2017; former manager of Juventus and other clubs; runs a vineyard and wine business in Brescia.

trajectory.event: Made his Serie A debut for Brescia on May 21, just two days after his 16th birthday, becoming the club's youngest ever debutant.
Won the Serie B title with Brescia, earning promotion to Serie A.
Signed for Serie A club Inter Milan, beginning his career at a top-tier club.
Won the UEFA Champions League with AC Milan, establishing himself as one of the world's best playmakers.
Won the FIFA World Cup with Italy, winning the Bronze Ball as the tournament's third-best player.
Joined Juventus on a free transfer and led them to four consecutive Serie A titles.
Retired from professional football after playing for New York City FC in MLS.

name: Yuan T. Lee
milestone_by_age_26: No material, independently verifiable milestone by age 26 found; he had completed his BS and MS degrees and was a first-year PhD student at UC Berkeley. His significant scientific contributions to crossed molecular beam techniques came during his PhD (completed 1965) and postdoctoral work (1967), and the Nobel Prize in Chemistry came in 1986 at age 50.

His significant scientific contributions came during and after his PhD work under Bruce Mahan.
family_context_summary: Born in Hsinchu, Taiwan in 1936 when the island was under Japanese occupation; inspired by the story of Marie Curie as a child. Father was a musician and keen sportsman.
evidence_summary: Yuan T. Lee was a first-year PhD student at UC Berkeley at age 26, having completed his BS in Taiwan and MS at Tsinghua. His significant scientific contributions to crossed molecular beam techniques came during his PhD (1965) and postdoctoral work with Dudley Herschbach (1967), leading to the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1986. No material milestone by age 26 was found.

name: Djamila Bouhired
milestone_by_age_26: Arrested in June 1957 at age 22 as a key FLN courier in the Algerian War of Independence; her trial, torture, and death sentence sparked an international campaign for her life, making her a globally recognized symbol of anti-colonial resistance.
early_history_summary: Born to a middle-class Muslim family in Algiers, Bouhired was educated in a French school where she rebelled against colonial identity. She joined the FLN at age 20 in 1954 when the revolution began, working as a liaison officer and assistant to FLN commander Yacef Saadi in Algiers, planting bombs and carrying documents.
family_context_summary: Born to a middle-class Muslim family in Algiers, French Algeria. She was educated in a French school where she was taught to identify as French but rebelled against this colonial identity from a young age.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources; family was middle-class and brothers were also involved in the underground struggle.
primary_early_advantage_tags: colonial oppression, FLN network, Algiers resistance, anti-colonial wave, middle-class education
evidence_summary: Djamila Bouhired was born to a middle-class Muslim family in Algiers and was educated in French schools where she developed anti-colonial consciousness. She joined the FLN at 20 when the Algerian revolution began, working as a courier and assistant to FLN commander Yacef Saadi. Her arrest, torture, and death sentence at 22 sparked an international campaign, making her a global symbol of the anti-colonial struggle. Her trajectory was shaped by direct immersion in colonial oppression and the Algerian resistance movement centered in Algiers.
starting_point: Born in June 1935 in Algiers, French Algeria, to a middle-class Muslim family; educated in French colonial schools where she developed early anti-colonial consciousness.
current_position: Living in Algeria at age 90; remains an icon of the Algerian independence movement.

trajectory.event: Joined the FLN at the outbreak of the Algerian War of Independence, working as a liaison officer in Algiers.
Arrested, tortured, and sentenced to death by French military court; her case sparked an international campaign for clemency.
Death sentence commuted to life imprisonment after global pressure on the French government.
Released from prison following Algerian independence and returned to Algiers as a national hero.
Married Jacques Verges, the French attorney who had defended her at trial.

name: Hermann Maier
milestone_by_age_26: Won two Olympic gold medals (super-G and giant slalom) at the 1998 Nagano Winter Olympics and claimed three World Cup titles in the 1997-98 season at age 25, despite having started World Cup racing only in 1996.
early_history_summary: Born in Flachau, Austria, to a ski school owner, Maier started skiing at age 3. He was accepted to the Austrian national ski academy at 15 but was dropped for being too small. He worked as a bricklayer and ski instructor for years before returning to competitive skiing at 22, winning his first World Cup race in 1997 at age 24.
family_context_summary: Born in Altenmarkt/Flachau, Austria; father Hermann Maier Sr. owned a skiing school in Flachau. Maier started skiing at age 3 and grew up in a town of 2,500 with five ski schools.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father owned a ski school in Flachau; Maier grew up immersed in skiing culture and worked as a ski instructor at his father's school during the winters.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Austrian skiing culture, father's ski school, Flachau skiing town, dismissed from academy, bricklayer comeback
evidence_summary: Hermann Maier was born into a skiing family in Flachau, Austria, where his father owned a ski school. He started skiing at 3 and showed superior technique early, but was dismissed from the Austrian national ski academy at 16 for being too small. He spent years as a bricklayer and ski instructor before returning to competitive skiing at 22, winning his first World Cup race at 24 and two Olympic golds at 25. His late breakthrough was driven by physical maturation after years of manual labor and persistent training at his father's ski school.
starting_point: Born in 1972 in Altenmarkt/Flachau, Austria; father owned a ski school; started skiing at age 3 in a town of 2,500 with five ski schools.
current_position: Retired from competitive skiing in 2009; manages the family ski school in Flachau, Austria.

trajectory.event: Accepted into the Austrian national ski academy at Schladming.
Dismissed from the ski academy due to slight build and knee problems; began working as a bricklayer's apprentice.
Earned his first World Cup points after returning to competitive skiing, winning the Europa Cup overall title.
Won his first World Cup race, a super-G at Garmisch-Partenkirchen, Germany.
Won two Olympic gold medals (super-G and giant slalom) at the Nagano Winter Olympics and claimed three World Cup titles.
Won two gold medals at the World Championships in Vail/Beaver Creek.
Nearly lost his right leg in a motorcycle accident, requiring a long recovery before returning to competitive skiing.
Won his fourth overall World Cup title, completing a remarkable comeback from the motorcycle accident.

name: Naoko Takeuchi
milestone_by_age_26: Launched Sailor Moon in Nakayoshi magazine in February 1992 at age 25, which became an instant hit, doubled the magazine's circulation from 1 to 2 million, spawned an anime adaptation within months, and won the 17th Kodansha Manga Award in 1993.
early_history_summary: Born in Kofu, Japan, to a family that ran a jewelry store, Takeuchi joined manga and astronomy clubs in high school. She debuted professionally with 'Love Call' in 1986 at age 19 while studying pharmacy at Kyoritsu College, then built her career through one-shots and serials before creating Codename: Sailor V in 1991, which she reworked into Sailor Moon.
family_context_summary: Born in Kofu, Yamanashi Prefecture, Japan; parents Kenji and Ikuko Takeuchi reportedly ran a jewelry store and were fairly wealthy. Her father encouraged her to pursue a backup career, leading her to study pharmacy at Kyoritsu College of Pharmacy.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources; parents ran a jewelry store but were not in the manga industry.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Japan manga ecosystem, Kodansha/Nakayoshi pipeline, wealthy family backup, early debut, magical girl wave
evidence_summary: Naoko Takeuchi was born to a wealthy family in Kofu, Japan, and developed a passion for manga from childhood. She debuted professionally at 19 with 'Love Call' while studying pharmacy as a backup career. Her editor at Nakayoshi, Fumio Osano, suggested the concept of a sailor-suited guardian of justice, which she developed into Codename: Sailor V and then Sailor Moon. The Sailor Moon manga launched in February 1992 and became an instant phenomenon, doubling Nakayoshi's circulation and spawning a massively successful anime franchise.
starting_point: Born in 1967 in Kofu, Yamanashi, Japan, to a fairly wealthy family that ran a jewelry store; father encouraged her to study pharmacy as a backup career.
current_position: Active manga artist; married to manga artist Yoshihiro Togashi since 1999; manages Sailor Moon properties through Princess Naoko Planning; living in Japan.

trajectory.event: Debuted as a manga artist with 'Love Call,' winning Nakayoshi's New Artist Award while still a university student.
Launched 'Codename: Sailor V' in Run-Run magazine, the precursor to Sailor Moon.
Launched Sailor Moon in Nakayoshi magazine, which became an instant hit and spawned an anime adaptation within months.
Won the 17th Kodansha Manga Award for Sailor Moon, cementing her status as a leading manga artist.
Concluded the Sailor Moon manga after 52 chapters and 18 volumes, with the franchise having sold tens of millions of copies worldwide.
Married manga artist Yoshihiro Togashi, creator of Yu Yu Hakusho and Hunter x Hunter.
